_source.description: Major global fluorspar (fluorite, CaF2) mining and production sites
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, Fluorspar chapter (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-fluorspar.pdf); British Geological Survey World Mineral Production 2019-2023 (https://www2.bgs.ac.uk/mineralsuk/statistics/worldStatistics.html); Orbia (formerly Mexichem) Annual Report 2023 (BMV: ORBIA); SepFluor Ltd corporate disclosures; Mongolrostsvetmet annual reports; China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association (CNIA) statistical yearbook; Minersa Group corporate publications; Kenya Fluorspar Company reports; Solvay SA Annual Report 2023 (EBR: SOLB); company annual reports and government mining department publications
_source.license: USGS: public domain; BGS: Open Government Licence; company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Major fluorspar operations globally. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company filings, and satellite verification. Production figures from USGS MCS 2024 (2023 data). China dominates global production (~64%) with operations spread across Inner Mongolia, Zhejiang, Fujian, Jiangxi, and Hunan provinces. CaF2 content grades reported where available.

_coverage.known_gaps: Numerous small Chinese operations not individually enumerated; some Iranian and North Korean production not tracked; artisanal operations in East Africa

sites.name: Sumoqagan Obo (Inner Mongolia)
sites.ownership: Inner Mongolia Xiang Zhen Mining Co.
sites.notes: One of China's largest fluorspar mining districts; Siziwang Banner; acid-grade and metallurgical-grade production

sites.name: Wulanhaote (Inner Mongolia)
sites.notes: Xing'an League fluorspar mining district; multiple underground mines

sites.name: Wuyishan (Fujian Province)
sites.notes: Fujian is China's second-largest fluorspar province; Wuyishan district includes multiple acid-grade producers

sites.name: Wuyi (Zhejiang Province)
sites.ownership: Zhejiang Wuyi Fluorite Mining Co. / various
sites.notes: Zhejiang's primary fluorspar district; historically one of China's earliest fluorspar mining regions; high-grade acid-spar

sites.name: Changning (Hunan Province)
sites.notes: Hunan Province is a major fluorspar producing area; Changning district supplies both acid-grade and metallurgical-grade fluorite

sites.name: Dexing (Jiangxi Province)
sites.notes: Jiangxi Province fluorspar district; significant acid-grade output; near major copper mining operations

sites.name: Xianghualing (Hunan Province)
sites.notes: Historic polymetallic district in Linwu County; fluorspar produced alongside tin-lead-zinc; skarn-type deposits

sites.name: Las Cuevas (San Luis Potosi)
sites.notes: World's largest single fluorspar mine; operated by Koura (Orbia's fluorinated solutions business); acid-grade CaF2 for HF production; underground mining

sites.name: Encantada-Buenavista (Coahuila)
sites.notes: Northern Mexico fluorspar district; multiple underground mines in Coahuila state; metallurgical and ceramic-grade production

sites.name: San Luis Potosi District
sites.notes: Broader San Luis Potosi mining district beyond Las Cuevas; multiple smaller operations producing metallurgical and acid-grade fluorspar

sites.name: Bor-Undur (Dundgovi)
sites.notes: Mongolia's largest fluorspar mine; Dundgovi province; produces high-purity acid-grade fluorite; exports primarily to Russia and China

sites.name: Berkh (Khentii)
sites.notes: Secondary fluorspar operation in Khentii province; acid-grade production

sites.name: Vergenoeg (Gauteng/Limpopo)
sites.notes: One of world's largest fluorspar deposits; unique fayalite-fluorite pipe deposit; open-pit mining with flotation to acid-grade; north of Pretoria

sites.name: Marico (North West Province)
sites.notes: North West Province operation; produces acid-grade and metallurgical-grade fluorspar

sites.name: Witkop (Limpopo)
sites.notes: Limpopo Province fluorspar mine; metallurgical and acid-grade production

sites.name: Nui Phao (Thai Nguyen)
sites.notes: Polymetallic mine producing fluorspar as significant by-product alongside tungsten concentrate; Thai Nguyen province; one of world's largest tungsten-fluorspar operations

sites.name: Asturias District
sites.notes: Spain's primary fluorspar producing region; Minersa operates multiple mines in Asturias including Villabona; acid-grade production for European chemical industry

sites.name: Berbes (Asturias)
sites.notes: Eastern Asturias fluorspar district; historic mining area famous for collector-quality fluorite specimens; active acid-grade production

sites.name: Kerio Valley (Kimwarer)
sites.ownership: Kenya Fluorspar Company (private; historically partly government-owned)
sites.notes: East Africa's only major fluorspar producer; Elgeyo-Marakwet County, Rift Valley; acid-grade production exported via Mombasa port

sites.name: Okorusu (Otjozondjupa)
sites.notes: Carbonatite-hosted fluorspar deposit; operated by Solvay until closure/sale; Otjiwarongo area; potential restart under new ownership

sites.name: El Hammam (Meknes)
sites.ownership: Managem Group (SNI/Al Mada, Moroccan royal holding)
sites.notes: Morocco's primary fluorspar operation; Meknes-Fes region; Samine produces acid-grade fluorite for export; underground mining

sites.name: Bahia District (Taquari-Vassouras)
sites.notes: Bahia state fluorspar operations; metallurgical and acid-grade production for domestic Brazilian market

sites.name: Peak District (Derbyshire)
sites.notes: Derbyshire's historic fluorspar mining district; UK's only significant fluorspar source; Cavendish Mill processing; Blue John variety historically famous

sites.name: Catamarca (Sierras Pampeanas)
sites.notes: Northwestern Argentina fluorspar district; Catamarca and San Luis provinces; small-scale production for domestic steel and chemical industries

sites.name: Isfahan District
sites.ownership: State and private Iranian mining companies
sites.notes: Central Iran fluorspar operations; multiple deposits in Isfahan and Markazi provinces; production primarily for domestic aluminum smelting and steel industries

sites.name: Erzgebirge (Saxony/Thuringia)
sites.notes: Ore Mountains (Erzgebirge) fluorspar-barite mining district; Germany's primary domestic fluorspar source; Niederschlag and Schoenbrunn deposits

sites.name: Speewah (Kimberley, WA)
sites.ownership: Thor Energy (formerly King River Resources subsidiary)
sites.notes: Large undeveloped fluorspar deposit in East Kimberley, Western Australia; PFS completed; potential to become one of world's largest fluorspar mines

sites.name: Palo Blanco (Durango)
sites.notes: Durango state fluorspar district; multiple underground mines; metallurgical-grade production

sites.name: St. Lawrence (Newfoundland)
sites.notes: Burin Peninsula, Newfoundland; AGS (acid-grade fluorspar) mine restarted 2018 after decades-long hiatus; North America's only primary fluorspar mine outside Mexico

sites.name: Perdhamkhan (Chhattisgarh)
sites.notes: Central India fluorspar deposits; Chhattisgarh and Gujarat states; production primarily for domestic aluminum and steel industries
